portInfo.description: Vigo is Galicia’s principal Atlantic cruise call. Ships dock at the Alberto Durán maritime station on Muelle de Trasatlánticos, one building shared by two concessionaires, and on multi-ship days at Muelle de Comercio (El Tinglado). Casco Vello, oyster bars, and the promenade are a short walk away.
portInfo.location: Northwest Spain (Galicia) on the Ría de Vigo
portInfo.language: Spanish and Galician; some English in tourist services

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Primary calls use Muelle de Trasatlánticos inside the Alberto Durán Maritime Station, where two concessioned terminals operate: Vigo Cruise Terminal and Atlantic Vigo Cruise Terminal (same building complex). Multi-ship days may also use El Tinglado on Muelle de Comercio.
transportation: Train station ~15 min walk (per port authority)
gettingThere.distanceToCity: Waterfront terminals sit beside the historic center—typically a few hundred meters to Casco Vello
gettingThere.walkingTime: Often 5–15 minutes uphill into the old town and commercial streets—confirm on your sailing programme before you rely on a fixed walk time.
gettingThere.taxiInfo: Taxis available at the maritime station area for Cíes ferry connections, Samil, or longer trips
gettingThere.publicTransport: Confirm local transport options with the ship on your call date.
gettingThere.distanceAnswer: Waterfront terminals sit beside the historic center—typically a few hundred meters to Casco Vello

thingsToDo.intro: Vigo is one of Spain’s most walkable Atlantic cruise calls: the Trasatlánticos waterfront sits beside Casco Vello. Save long transfers for Cíes or Santiago only when time truly allows.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Uphill lanes in Casco Vello take longer than the map suggests. Wear comfortable shoes and keep an eye on ship time even though the pier is close.
